questions.prompt: Are there good work opportunities in your home country?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I work. My country has work.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I think so. There are jobs in my country, and my family works. But sometimes it is difficult to find a good job, because many people want to work.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think there are some good work opportunities in my country, especially in the cities. For example, you can find jobs in offices or in shops. However, it can be difficult to find a really good job with good pay. Also, a lot of people are looking for work, so there's competition.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, it's a bit of a mixed bag. In the bigger cities there's a growing number of jobs cropping up in IT and services, so people with the right skills can land a decent job fairly easily. That said, in rural areas things are much tougher, and plenty of youngsters end up going abroad to make ends meet.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men ishlayman. Mening davlatimda ish bor.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men shunday deb o'ylayman. Mening mamlakatimda ish o'rinlari bor va mening oilam ishlaydi. Lekin ba'zan yaxshi ish topish qiyin, chunki ko'p odamlar ishlashni xohlashadi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, menimcha, mening mamlakatimda yaxshi ish imkoniyatlari bor, ayniqsa shaharlarda. Misol uchun, ofislarda yoki do'konlarda ish topishingiz mumkin. Biroq, yaxshi maoshli haqiqatan ham yaxshi ish topish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ko'p odamlar ish qidirmoqda, shuning uchun raqobat bor.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Menimcha, imkoniyatlar, albatta, bor, lekin bu soha va joylashuvga bog'liq. Katta shaharlarda texnologiya va moliya sohalarida o'sib borayotgan ish o'rinlarini topishingiz mumkin.
Biroq, qishloq joylarda imkoniyatlar cheklanganroq va odamlar yaxshiroq istiqbollarni topish uchun ko'chishga majbur bo'lishadi. Hukumat investitsiyalarni rag'batlantirish va ko'proq ish o'rinlarini yaratishga harakat qilayotgan bo'lsa-da, bandlik masalasida shahar va qishloq joylari o'rtasida sezilarli farq mavjud.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Are there good work opportunities in your home country?
idioms: the grass is always greener on the other side - "boshqaning tomorqasi yashilroq ko'rinadi"
sentenceStarters: "I'd say the situation is mixed…" - "Menimcha, vaziyat aralash…"
"In recent years, the government has been actively…" - "So'nggi yillarda hukumat faol ravishda…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd say the situation is mixed, to be honest. In recent years, the government has been actively trying to create more job opportunities, especially in the IT and service sectors, and there's been a noticeable growth in start-ups and small businesses.
However, in many rural areas, finding well-paid work is still quite challenging. A lot of young people move to bigger cities or even go abroad to pursue better prospects. I think there's potential, but the job market still has a long way to go.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, vaziyat aralash deb aytgan bo'lardim. So'nggi yillarda hukumat, ayniqsa IT va xizmat ko'rsatish sohalarida, ko'proq ish o'rinlari yaratishga faol harakat qilmoqda va startaplar va kichik biznesda sezilarli o'sish kuzatilmoqda.

Biroq, ko'plab qishloq joylarda yaxshi maoshli ish topish hali ham ancha qiyin. Ko'p yoshlar katta shaharlarga ko'chib o'tishadi yoki hatto yaxshiroq istiqbollarni izlash uchun chet elga ketishadi. Menimcha, imkoniyat bor, lekin mehnat bozori hali uzoq yo'lni bosib o'tishi kerak.

questions.prompt: Has your life changed much in the last year?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I have a new job. I am happy. It is good.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, my life is different. I moved to a new house and it is bigger than my old house. I like it but it is far from my work. So, I wake up early.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, my life has changed a bit in the last year. I started learning a new language, which is quite challenging, but also very rewarding. I think it's good to learn new things. Also, I went on a nice holiday with my family. However, I still have the same job and the same friends.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, quite a bit, actually. The biggest change is that I've really knuckled down with my studies and started setting clear goals for myself. I suppose I've also become far more independent — I've learnt to manage my time properly. Looking back, these little changes have honestly helped me grow as a person.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Menda yangi ish bor. Men xursandman. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, hayotim o'zgardi. Men yangi uyga ko'chib o'tdim va u eski uyimdan kattaroq. Menga yoqadi, lekin u ishimdan uzoqda. Shuning uchun, men erta turaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, hayotim o'tgan yili biroz o'zgardi. Men yangi til o'rganishni boshladim, bu ancha qiyin, lekin juda foydali ham. O'ylaymanki, yangi narsalarni o'rganish yaxshi. Shuningdek, oilam bilan yaxshi ta'tilga bordim.
Biroq, men hali ham o'sha ishda ishlayman va o'sha do'stlarim bor.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, menimcha, hayotim o'tgan yili biroz o'zgardi. Men o'z sog'lig'im va farovonligimni birinchi o'ringa qo'yishga qaror qildim, shuning uchun muntazam mashqlar va sog'lom ovqatlanishni kundalik hayotimga kiritdim. Bu mening energiya darajamni va umumiy kayfiyatimni sezilarli darajada yaxshiladi. Bundan tashqari, men jamiyat loyihalarida faolroq ishtirok eta boshladim, bu esa dunyoqarashimni kengaytirdi va menga maqsad tuyg'usini berdi. Bu o'zgarishlar keskin bo'lmagan bo'lsa-da, ular albatta ijobiy va ta'sirli bo'ldi.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Has your life changed much in the last year?
idioms: turn over a new leaf - "yangi sahifa ochmoq"
every cloud has a silver lining - "har bir qorong'ulikning ortida yorug'lik bor"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I'd say my life has changed quite significantly…" - "Ha, menimcha hayotim sezilarli darajada o'zgardi…"
"Looking back, I think these changes have been…" - "Orqaga qarab, menimcha bu o'zgarishlar…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I'd say my life has changed quite significantly over the past year. I started taking my studies more seriously and set some clear personal goals, which has really helped me become more organised and focused.
I've also become more independent — I've learned to manage my time better and take on more responsibilities. Looking back, I think these changes have been overwhelmingly positive and have helped me grow as a person.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, menimcha, hayotim o'tgan yil davomida ancha sezilarli darajada o'zgardi. Men o'qishlarimga jiddiyroq yondasha boshladim va shaxsiy maqsadlarimni aniq belgilab oldim, bu esa menga yanada tartibli va diqqatli bo'lishimga juda yordam berdi.

Men ham mustaqilroq bo'lib qoldim — vaqtimni yaxshiroq boshqarishni va ko'proq mas'uliyatni o'z zimmamga olishni o'rgandim. O'tmishga nazar tashlasam, bu o'zgarishlar asosan ijobiy bo'ldi va shaxs sifatida o'sishimga yordam berdi deb o'ylayman.

questions.prompt: Is it easy for you to make new friends?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like new friends. I play with them. Happy.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I think it is easy. I like to talk to people and I ask them questions. Sometimes they are nice and we play together. But sometimes they don't want to be friends.
questions.sampleB1: I think it's quite easy for me to make new friends. I'm usually friendly and I try to be open to meeting new people. For example, if I see someone at a club with a shared interest, I might start a conversation. However, it's not always easy to maintain those friendships later on.
questions.sampleB2: I'd say it really depends on the setting. I'm a pretty sociable person, so in relaxed places like a party I find it easy to strike up a conversation and break the ice. That said, I'm not one to approach strangers out of the blue. The thing is, a real friendship takes time — you need to build mutual trust and find some common ground.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Menga yangi do'stlar yoqadi. Men ular bilan o'ynayman. Xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menimcha bu oson. Men odamlar bilan gaplashishni yaxshi ko'raman va ularga savollar beraman. Ba'zan ular yaxshi bo'lishadi va biz birga o'ynaymiz. Lekin ba'zan ular do'st bo'lishni xohlashmaydi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Menimcha, yangi do'stlar orttirish men uchun ancha oson. Men odatda do'stona bo'laman va yangi odamlar bilan tanishishga ochiq bo'lishga harakat qilaman. Masalan, agar men klubda umumiy qiziqishga ega bo'lgan odamni ko'rsam, men suhbatni boshlashim mumkin. Biroq, keyinchalik bu do'stliklarni saqlab qolish har doim ham oson emas.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men bu oson deb ayta olmayman, lekin men odatda dastlabki aloqalarni o'rnatishni yetarlicha oson deb bilaman. Men ancha kirishimli odamman va qiziqarli ko'ringan yoki o'xshash ishtiyoqlarga ega bo'lgan odamlarga intilishga moyilman. Biroq, tanishdan haqiqiy do'stga o'tish qiyinroq bo'ladi. Bu doimiy harakat, zaiflik va munosabatlarni rivojlantirishga vaqt ajratishga tayyorlikni talab qiladi. Shunday qilib, yangi odamlar bilan tanishish unchalik qiyin bo'lmasa-da, chuqur do'stlik o'rnatish butunlay boshqa masala.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Is it easy for you to make new friends?
idioms: a friend in need is a friend indeed - "haqiqiy do'st — boshingga mushkul tushganda bilinar"
sentenceStarters: "I'd say it depends on the situation…" - "Menimcha, bu vaziyatga bog'liq…"
"I think building a real friendship takes time…" - "Menimcha, haqiqiy do'stlik qurish vaqt talab qiladi…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd say it depends on the situation. I'm generally quite a sociable person, so in relaxed settings like a party or a group activity, I find it relatively easy to strike up a conversation with new people.
However, I'm not the type to approach strangers out of the blue. I think building a real friendship takes time — it's not just about meeting someone once, it's about developing mutual trust and finding common ground.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, vaziyatga bog'liq. Men odatda juda kirishimli odamman, shuning uchun ziyofat yoki guruh mashg'ulotlari kabi erkin muhitlarda yangi odamlar bilan nisbatan oson suhbat boshlay olaman.

Biroq, men birdaniga notanish odamlarga yaqinlashadigan odam emasman. O'ylashimcha, haqiqiy do'stlik qurish vaqt talab etadi — bu shunchaki bir marta kim bilandir tanishish emas, balki o'zaro ishonchni rivojlantirish va umumiy til topishdir.

questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, I can see a modern kitchen where a family is cooking a stir-fry with a robotic arm lending a hand. A young man is tossing in some red peppers while a woman chops herbs, and everyone looks cheerful. In the second one, an Uzbek family is making manti dumplings by hand — the grandfather in a skullcap is loading the steamer while the mother fills the dough. The striking contrast here is between cutting-edge technology and time-honoured methods passed down through generations.

Bu qarama-qarshilik kulinar amaliyotlarning evolyutsiyasini va zamonaviy innovatsiyalarning qadimiy usullar bilan uyg'unligini ta'kidlaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?

questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first picture, I can see people preparing food with the help of a robot. It looks like a modern, highly technological kitchen where machines are assisting in the cooking process, which suggests a futuristic approach to meal preparation.
In the second picture, people are cooking a traditional meal by hand, using time-honoured methods. The contrast between the two images highlights the difference between modern innovation and traditional culinary practices.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda odamlarning robot yordamida ovqat tayyorlayotganini ko'rishim mumkin. Bu zamonaviy, juda texnologik oshxonaga o'xshaydi, u yerda mashinalar ovqat pishirish jarayonida yordam bermoqda, bu esa taom tayyorlashga futuristik yondashuvni taklif qiladi.

Ikkinchi rasmda odamlar an'anaviy taomni qo'lda, qadimiy usullar yordamida tayyorlashmoqda. Ikkala rasm o'rtasidagi farq zamonaviy innovatsiyalar va an'anaviy pazandachilik amaliyotlari o'rtasidagi farqni ta'kidlaydi.

questions.prompt: Is technology making cooking better or worse?
questions.sampleA1: I like cooking. Technology... good. I have a phone. I look recipe.
questions.sampleA2: I think technology is good for cooking. Because I can find recipes on the internet. And I can watch videos. But sometimes it's difficult. My mom says the old way is better.
questions.sampleB1: In my opinion, technology is making cooking better. For example, I can easily find recipes online. Also, kitchen appliances are more advanced now. However, some people might say it's making cooking worse because they don't learn traditional skills anymore. I think it's mostly positive though.
questions.sampleB2: On the whole, I reckon technology is making cooking better, though it's a bit of a double-edged sword. Smart appliances and online recipes have made meals faster and opened up whole new cuisines to us. The downside, though, is that people are gradually losing those hands-on skills. So ideally, tech should complement traditional cooking rather than take it over.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men ovqat pishirishni yaxshi ko'raman. Texnologiya... yaxshi. Menda telefon bor. Men retsept qidiraman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, texnologiya ovqat pishirish uchun yaxshi. Chunki internetdan retseptlar topishim mumkin. Va videolarni ko'rishim mumkin. Lekin ba'zida qiyin bo'ladi. Onamning aytishicha, eski usul yaxshiroq.
questions.uzSampleB1: Mening fikrimcha, texnologiya ovqat pishirishni yaxshilamoqda. Misol uchun, men retseptlarni onlaynda osongina topa olaman. Shuningdek, oshxona jihozlari hozir ancha rivojlangan. Biroq, ba'zi odamlar bu ovqat pishirishni yomonlashtirmoqda deyishi mumkin, chunki ular endi an'anaviy ko'nikmalarni o'rganmayaptilar. Menimcha, bu asosan ijobiy.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men texnologiya ba'zi kamchiliklarga qaramay, asosan, pishirish tajribasini yaxshilayapti, deb bahslashardim. Onlayn retseptlar va qo'llanmalarning ommabopligi oshpazlik bilimlarini demokratlashtirdi. Zamonaviy jihozlar ham jarayonlarni soddalashtiradi, vaqt va kuchni tejaydi.

Biroq, texnologiyaga tayanish an'anaviy pishirish mahoratini kamaytiradi va ovqat tayyorlashning ijtimoiy jihatini qisqartiradi, degan asosli xavotir bor. Odamlar oldindan qadoqlangan yechimlar yoki avtomatlashtirilgan qurilmalarga haddan tashqari bog'lanib qolishi mumkin.

Oxir-oqibat, men muvozanatli yondashuv muhim, deb hisoblayman. Texnologiya pishirishning asosiy tamoyillarini va umumiy oshpazlik tajribalarining qadrini almashtirmasligi, balki yaxshilashi kerak.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Is technology making cooking better or worse?
idioms: the best of both worlds - "ikkala dunyoning eng yaxshisi"
you can't make an omelette without breaking eggs - "tuxum sindimasdan omlet qilib bo'lmaydi"
sentenceStarters: "I believe technology is largely making cooking better…" - "Menimcha, texnologiya asosan ovqat pishirishni yaxshilamoqda…"
"In my view, technology should complement…" - "Menimcha, texnologiya … ni to'ldirishi kerak"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I believe technology is largely making cooking better, although it's a double-edged sword. On the positive side, modern kitchen gadgets and smart appliances have made meal preparation faster and more energy-efficient. Apps and online recipes give people access to thousands of dishes from around the world, which significantly expands our culinary horizons.
However, there's a downside. As people rely more on technology, many are losing the hands-on skills that were once passed down through generations. Cooking used to be a social activity — families would gather in the kitchen and share knowledge. Now, some people just press a button on a machine and call it dinner.
In my view, technology should complement traditional cooking rather than replace it. As the saying goes, "the best of both worlds" — we can enjoy modern convenience while still preserving the art of cooking by hand.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, texnologiya asosan ovqat pishirishni yaxshilamoqda, garchi bu ikki tomonlama qilich bo'lsa ham. Ijobiy tomoni shundaki, zamonaviy oshxona anjomlari va aqlli jihozlar ovqat tayyorlashni tezroq va energiya jihatidan samaraliroq qildi. Ilovalar va onlayn retseptlar odamlarga butun dunyo bo'ylab minglab taomlarga kirish imkonini beradi, bu bizning kulinar ufqlarimizni sezilarli darajada kengaytiradi.

Biroq, salbiy tomoni ham bor. Odamlar texnologiyaga ko'proq tayangan sari, ko'pchilik avloddan-avlodga o'tib kelgan amaliy ko'nikmalarni yo'qotmoqda. Ovqat pishirish ilgari ijtimoiy faoliyat edi - oilalar oshxonada yig'ilib, bilimlarini baham ko'rishardi. Endi ba'zi odamlar shunchaki mashinadagi tugmani bosib, buni kechki ovqat deb atashadi.

Menimcha, texnologiya an'anaviy ovqat pishirishni almashtirishdan ko'ra, uni to'ldirishi kerak. Aytishlaricha, "ikki dunyoning eng yaxshisi" - biz zamonaviy qulayliklardan bahramand bo'lishimiz, shu bilan birga qo'lda ovqat pishirish san'atini saqlab qolishimiz mumkin.

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer traditional methods?
questions.sampleA1: I like old ways. My grandma cooks good. It is nice.
questions.sampleA2: Some people like old ways because they are easy. And they know them. But new ways are good too, I think.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think some people prefer traditional methods because they are used to them. For example, my grandmother always cooks in a certain way. Also, maybe they think it's better quality or more authentic. However, new methods can be good too, it depends.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I suppose there are a few reasons. For a lot of people, cooking the old way is a way to preserve cultural heritage and stay connected to their roots. Others simply believe food made by hand has a certain personal touch that machines can't match. And some folks are set in their ways — as they say, if it ain't broke, don't fix it.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga eski usullar yoqadi. Mening buvim yaxshi ovqat pishiradi. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ba'zi odamlar eski usullarni yaxshi ko'radilar, chunki ular oson. Va ular ularni bilishadi. Lekin yangi usullar ham yaxshi, menimcha.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, ba'zi odamlar an'anaviy usullarni afzal ko'rishadi, chunki ular bunga o'rganib qolishgan.
Masalan, buvim har doim ma'lum bir usulda ovqat pishiradi. Shuningdek, ehtimol, ular buni sifatliroq yoki haqiqiyroq deb o'ylashadi.
Biroq, yangi usullar ham yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin, bu narsaga bog'liq.
questions.uzSampleB2: Odamlar an'anaviy usullarni afzal ko'rishlarining bir nechta sabablari bo'lishi mumkin. Ehtimol, ular o'tmish bilan kuchliroq aloqani his qilishadi va o'sha aloqalarni saqlab qolishni xohlashadi. Ular, shuningdek, an'anaviy texnikalar yuqori natija berishiga ishonishlari mumkin, bu ovqat pishirishda bo'ladimi yoki hunarmandchilikda. Bundan tashqari, ba'zi odamlar o'zgarishga tabiiy ravishda qarshilik ko'rsatadilar va tanish va yaxshi o'rnatilgan ishlash usullarida o'zlarini qulay his qilishadi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do some people prefer traditional methods?
idioms: old ways are the best ways - "eski usullar — eng yaxshi usullar"
if it ain't broke, don't fix it - "buzilmagan bo'lsa, tuzatma"
sentenceStarters: "There are several reasons why many people still prefer…" - "Ko'p odamlar hali ham … ni afzal ko'rishining bir nechta sababi bor"
"Many people believe that food prepared by hand…" - "Ko'pchilik qo'l bilan tayyorlangan ovqat … deb hisoblaydi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several reasons why many people still prefer traditional cooking methods. Firstly, traditional cooking is often seen as a way to preserve cultural heritage. Recipes passed down through generations carry deep personal and cultural meaning — they connect people to their roots and their family history.
Secondly, many people believe that food prepared by hand simply tastes better. There's a certain warmth and personal touch in homemade food that machines simply cannot replicate. The process of cooking itself can be therapeutic — kneading dough, stirring a pot, and seasoning by taste are all deeply satisfying experiences.
Finally, some people distrust technology in the kitchen because they feel it takes away control and creativity. As they say, "old ways are the best ways" — for many, the charm of cooking lies in doing it with your own two hands.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ko'pchilik odamlarning an'anaviy pishirish usullarini afzal ko'rishlarining bir nechta sabablari bor. Birinchidan, an'anaviy pishirish ko'pincha madaniy merosni saqlash usuli sifatida qaraladi. Avloddan-avlodga o'tib kelayotgan retseptlar chuqur shaxsiy va madaniy ma'noga ega — ular odamlarni o'z ildizlari va oila tarixi bilan bog'laydi.

Ikkinchidan, ko'pchilik qo'lda tayyorlangan ovqat shunchaki mazaliroq bo'lishiga ishonadi. Uyda tayyorlangan ovqatda o'ziga xos iliqlik va shaxsiy teginish bor, uni mashinalar takrorlay olmaydi. Pishirish jarayonining o'zi terapevtik bo'lishi mumkin — xamir qorish, qozonni aralashtirish va ta'bga ko'ra ziravorlar qo'shish juda qoniqarli tajribalardir.

Nihoyat, ba'zi odamlar oshxonadagi texnologiyaga ishonmaydi, chunki ular bu nazorat va ijodkorlikni olib qo'yadi deb hisoblashadi. Aytishlaricha, "eski yo'llar eng yaxshi yo'llardir" — ko'pchilik uchun pishirishning jozibasi uni o'z qo'llaringiz bilan qilishda.

questions.prompt: Share a time when silence helped you understand something better.
questions.sampleA2: I remember one time. I was quiet and then I understand. My friend was sad, but I didn't know. But I see her face and I understand she is sad.
questions.sampleB1: Once, I was in a meeting, and everyone was talking. I didn't understand the problem. Then I was quiet and I listened. I started to understand what they were saying and I had an idea. I think silence helped me understand better.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, this is something I feel quite strongly about. I'd like to share an experience from last year, when I had a massive falling-out with one of my closest friends. My first instinct was to fire back and say something I'd probably regret, but instead I chose to hold my tongue and give myself some time to reflect. During that quiet spell, it gradually dawned on me that the whole argument came down to a simple misunderstanding, and my friend hadn't meant any harm at all. That silence gave me the clarity I needed to patch things up calmly. The thing is, silence has genuinely shaped my personal growth. I've come to realise that not every situation calls for an immediate reaction — sometimes stepping back and thinking things through leads to far wiser decisions. It's taught me patience and a good deal of emotional intelligence, which I was honestly lacking before. These days, I make a point of pausing before I speak, and it's made a real difference in how I get on with people. On a wider level, I suppose silence can be incredibly valuable in society too. In classrooms, a few quiet moments let students absorb information and actually think for themselves. In busy workplaces, a bit of calm reflection often produces far more thoughtful choices than rushing in. As the old saying goes, silence is golden — in a world that never seems to quieten down, the ability to simply sit still and listen is a genuinely rare and precious skill.
questions.uzSampleA2: Esimda bir vaqt bor. Men jim edim va keyin tushundim. Do'stim xafa edi, lekin men bilmasdim. Lekin men uning yuzini ko'rdim va u xafa ekanligini tushundim.
questions.uzSampleB1: Bir marta men yig'ilishda edim va hamma gapirayotgan edi. Men muammoni tushunmadim. Keyin men jim bo'ldim va tingladim. Men ularning nima deyayotganini tushuna boshladim va menda bir fikr paydo bo'ldi. O'ylaymanki, jimlik menga yaxshiroq tushunishga yordam berdi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Esimda, men yangi mahorat o'rganayotgan edim, gitara chalishni. Men asabiylashayotgan edim, chunki yaxshilanmayotgan edim. Keyin men tanaffus qilishga va bir muddat jim bo'lishga qaror qildim. O'sha sukut davomida men tezlikka juda ko'p e'tibor qaratayotganimni va aniqlikka yetarli emasligini angladim. Qayta chalishni boshlaganimda, men ancha e'tiborli edim va tezda yaxshiladim. Shunday qilib, sukut menga nima noto'g'ri qilayotganimni tushunishga yordam berdi.

bulletPoints: Share a time when silence helped you understand something better.
How has silence affected your personal growth?
How can silence be useful in society?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time when silence helped me:
I'd like to share an experience from last year when I had a major disagreement with a close friend. Instead of reacting immediately and saying something I might regret, I chose to stay silent and take some time to reflect. During that quiet period, I gradually realised that the argument was based on a simple misunderstanding, and my friend hadn't meant any harm. That silence gave me the clarity I needed to approach the situation calmly.
How silence has affected my personal growth:
Silence has profoundly affected my personal growth. I've learned that not every situation requires an immediate response — sometimes, stepping back and thinking things through leads to much better decisions. It has helped me develop patience, emotional intelligence, and a deeper understanding of myself and others.
How silence can be useful in society:
In broader society, silence can be incredibly powerful. In education, moments of silence allow students to absorb information and think critically. In workplaces, quiet reflection can lead to more thoughtful decisions. As the proverb says, "silence is golden" — in a world full of noise, the ability to be still and think is a truly valuable skill.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Sukut menga yordam bergan vaqt:
O'tgan yili yaqin do'stim bilan katta kelishmovchilik bo'lgan voqeani baham ko'rmoqchiman. Darhol javob berish va afsuslanadigan gaplarni aytish o'rniga, men sukut saqlashni va biroz vaqt ajratib, fikrlashni tanladim. O'sha sokin davrda men asta-sekin angladimki, bahs oddiy tushunmovchilikka asoslangan ekan va do'stim hech qanday yomon niyat qilmagan ekan. O'sha sukut menga vaziyatga xotirjamlik bilan yondashishim uchun zarur bo'lgan aniqlikni berdi.
Sukutning shaxsiy o'sishimga ta'siri:
Sukut mening shaxsiy o'sishimga juda katta ta'sir ko'rsatdi. Men har bir vaziyat darhol javob berishni talab qilmasligini o'rgandim — ba'zan, orqaga chekinib, narsalar haqida o'ylab ko'rish ancha yaxshi qarorlarga olib keladi. Bu menga sabr-toqatni, hissiy intellektni va o'zimni va boshqalarni chuqurroq tushunishni rivojlantirishga yordam berdi.
Sukut jamiyatda qanday foydali bo'lishi mumkin:
Kengroq jamiyatda sukut juda kuchli bo'lishi mumkin. Ta'limda sukut daqiqalari talabalarga ma'lumotni o'zlashtirishga va tanqidiy fikrlashga imkon beradi. Ish joylarida sokin mulohaza yuritish yanada o'ylangan qarorlarga olib kelishi mumkin. Maqolda aytilganidek, "sukut — oltin" — shovqinga to'la dunyoda tinch turish va o'ylash qobiliyati haqiqatan ham qimmatli mahoratdir.

questions.prompt: Strict global rules are needed right now to stop climate change.
questions.sampleA1: Climate change bad. Rules good. Help planet.
questions.sampleA2: I think climate change is a problem. Rules can help, and maybe it's good. But rules are difficult, because some countries don't like it.
questions.sampleB1: I think climate change is a very big problem. So, in my opinion, rules are important to stop it. For example, we can use less plastic and drive less. However, some people don't like rules because they are expensive. But I think we need to do something for the future.
questions.sampleB2: Well, this is an extremely important and timely debate, and to be honest I can see both sides of it. Those in favour of strict global rules argue that climate change is a shared responsibility that no single country can tackle on its own. By bringing in binding regulations, governments would be forced to pull together and cooperate. On top of that, such rules would push companies to speed up the development of clean technologies, which could actually create brand-new industries and jobs in the long run. Having said that, the other side raises some pretty compelling arguments. Shutting down older industries like coal and oil could leave millions of workers out of work, especially in regions that lean heavily on those sectors. Strict rules would also drive up the price of everyday essentials like heating and electricity, placing a disproportionate burden on ordinary families. And developing nations quite rightly point out that these rules could hinder economic growth just when they need it most. After all, it hardly seems fair to ask countries that are still developing to sacrifice their progress for a crisis they did very little to create. Personally, I do think we urgently need global cooperation, but the rules have to be fair and flexible. The wealthier countries, which caused most of the damage, should really foot the bill and help poorer ones make the switch. As the saying goes, there's no planet B — so we simply have to act, but in a way that doesn't leave the most vulnerable behind.
questions.uzSampleA1: Iqlim o'zgarishi yomon. Qoidalar yaxshi. Planetaga yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, iqlim o'zgarishi muammo. Qoidalar yordam berishi mumkin, va balki bu yaxshidir. Lekin qoidalar qiyin, chunki ba'zi davlatlarga bu yoqmaydi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Menimcha, iqlim o'zgarishi juda katta muammo. Shuning uchun, mening fikrimcha, uni to'xtatish uchun qoidalar muhim. Masalan, biz kamroq plastikdan foydalanishimiz va kamroq mashina haydashimiz mumkin. Biroq, ba'zi odamlarga qoidalar yoqmaydi, chunki ular qimmat. Lekin menimcha, kelajak uchun biror narsa qilishimiz kerak.
questions.uzSampleB2: Iqlim o'zgarishi jiddiy tahdid ekanligi aniq va menimcha, unga samarali yechim topish uchun global qoidalar zarur. Bu qoidalar davlatlarni o'z chiqindilarini kamaytirishga va qayta tiklanadigan energiyaga sarmoya kiritishga undashi mumkin. Biroq, potentsial kamchiliklar ham mavjud. Misol uchun, qat'iy qoidalar ba'zi iqtisodiyotlarga, ayniqsa qazilma yoqilg'iga juda bog'liq bo'lganlarga salbiy ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin. Atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish va iqtisodiy barqarorlik o'rtasida muvozanatni topish muhim, ehtimol toza energiya manbalariga o'tayotgan davlatlarga moliyaviy yordam berish orqali.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is an extremely important and timely debate. Advocates of strict global rules argue that climate change is a shared responsibility that no single country can tackle alone. By enforcing binding regulations, nations would be forced to cooperate and work as a team. These rules would also push businesses to innovate and develop clean technologies more rapidly, which could create new industries and jobs in the long run.
However, the opposing side raises some compelling arguments. Shutting down major industries like coal and oil could leave millions of workers unemployed, particularly in regions that depend heavily on these sectors. Stricter regulations would also drive up the cost of basic necessities like heating and electricity, placing a disproportionate burden on lower-income families. Furthermore, developing countries argue that such rules would hinder economic growth at a time when they need it most.
In my opinion, we absolutely need global cooperation to address climate change, but these rules must be fair and flexible. As the saying goes, "we do not inherit the earth from our ancestors, we borrow it from our children" — we must act, but in a way that doesn't leave the most vulnerable behind.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu juda muhim va o'z vaqtida ko'tarilgan bahs. Qattiq global qoidalarni yoqlovchilarning ta'kidlashicha, iqlim o'zgarishi - bu hech bir davlat yolg'iz uddalay olmaydigan umumiy mas'uliyatdir. Majburiy qoidalarni joriy etish orqali davlatlar hamkorlik qilishga va bir jamoa bo'lib ishlashga majbur bo'ladi. Ushbu qoidalar, shuningdek, korxonalarni innovatsiyalar yaratishga va uzoq muddatda yangi sanoat va ish o'rinlarini yaratishi mumkin bo'lgan toza texnologiyalarni tezroq rivojlantirishga undaydi.

Biroq, qarshi tomon ba'zi ishonarli dalillarni keltirmoqda. Ko'mir va neft kabi yirik sanoat tarmoqlarini yopish millionlab ishchilarni ishsiz qoldirishi mumkin, ayniqsa ushbu sohalarga juda bog'liq bo'lgan hududlarda. Qattiqroq qoidalar, shuningdek, isitish va elektr energiyasi kabi asosiy ehtiyojlarning narxini oshiradi va kam daromadli oilalarga nomutanosib yukni yuklaydi. Bundan tashqari, rivojlanayotgan davlatlar bunday qoidalar ular eng muhtoj bo'lgan paytda iqtisodiy o'sishga to'sqinlik qiladi, deb ta'kidlamoqda.

Menimcha, iqlim o'zgarishiga qarshi kurashish uchun bizga albatta global hamkorlik kerak, ammo bu qoidalar adolatli va moslashuvchan bo'lishi kerak. Aytishlaricha, "biz yer yuzini ota-bobolarimizdan meros qilib olmaymiz, uni farzandlarimizdan qarzga olamiz" — biz harakat qilishimiz kerak, lekin eng zaif qatlamlarni ortda qoldirmaydigan tarzda.
